main_text.p: gnoscit, atque etiam obligare: sed ob illorum jurium plerumque incertitudinem, merito dubitari potest, quatenus obligent. Dicendum est, obligari subditum indubie ad confervandum quantum in ipso est omnia jura quae νόμῳ aut ἔθῳ[?], legibus aut moribus constat esse legitima; id est quae aut jure scripto definita sunt, aut longo temporis usu & diuturna (ut vocant) præscriptione invaluerunt: quatenus sc. ii nota sunt, vel etiam posthac moraliter innotescere poterint. Non tamen pariter obligari ad omnia ea observanda quae sunt dubii aut controversi juris: præsertim cum soleant fere vi potestate præditi funiculos agrorum extendere, & ultra lapides clientium salire, nec jurium suorum finibus contenti esse. Debet tamen subditus animo esse semper parato, & illa quae sunt dubia, ubi justa esse constiterit, agnoscere & tueri.
main_text.head: SECT. XVIII.
main_text.p: Ultimus Casus est, ubi exigitur Ju-Casus 16ramentum a membro alicujus communitatis, puta Civitatis, Academiæ, Collegii, aut societatis Mercatorum vel Artificum,

page.notes: The left margin is clipped by the scan edge: the first letters of several lines (e.g. "gnoscit", "illorum", "nem", "jurium") are partly cut off; they were read from the visible remainder and the reconstruction is as printed. Greek "νόμῳ" and the second Greek word ("ἔθῳ") are read from a small, faint print; the second Greek word is doubtful. "ui" was printed for the ablative "vi" and is corrected to "vi" under the u/v rule. The last line "tificum," is the end of "Artificum," split at the line end. The marginal note "Casus 16" is in the right margin beside "Ultimus Casus". Show-through and the "§9" page marker are otherwise left as seen.
